entries.title: Ohm's Law
entries.content: Ohm's Law states that voltage across a conductor equals current times resistance. V = I×R, I = V/R, R = V/I. Example: 12V across 6Ω draws 2A. It is the foundation of circuit analysis. Units: Volt (V), Ampere (A), Ohm (Ω). Note: applies to ohmic (linear) conductors at constant temperature.

entries.title: Electrical Power
entries.formula: P = V × I = I² × R = V²/R
entries.content: Electrical power is the rate of energy transfer. P = V×I (watts). Also P = I²R and P = V²/R. 1 kW running 1 hour = 1 unit (kWh) of electricity. Energy in kWh = Power(W) × hours / 1000.

entries.title: Kirchhoff's Laws
entries.content: KCL (Current Law): sum of currents entering a node equals sum leaving — charge is conserved. KVL (Voltage Law): sum of voltages around any closed loop is zero — energy is conserved. Together they solve any resistive network.

entries.title: AC vs DC
entries.content: DC (Direct Current) flows in one direction — batteries, USB, electronics. AC (Alternating Current) reverses direction periodically — grid supply (50Hz in India, 60Hz in USA). AC is used for transmission because transformers step voltage up/down easily, reducing line losses.

entries.title: Transformer
entries.content: A transformer transfers AC energy between circuits via electromagnetic induction, with no moving parts. Step-up increases voltage (Ns > Np), step-down decreases it. Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = Ip/Is (inverse for current). Works only with AC.

entries.title: Power Factor
entries.content: Power factor is the ratio of real power (kW) to apparent power (kVA), equal to cos(φ) of the phase angle. PF = 1 is ideal (pure resistive). Inductive loads (motors) lower the PF; capacitor banks correct it. Low PF means higher current for the same useful power — utilities penalize it.

entries.title: Earthing / Grounding
entries.content: Earthing connects electrical installations to the ground so fault current safely flows to earth, tripping protective devices. Types: plate earthing, pipe earthing, rod earthing. Typical residential earth resistance should be below 5 Ω. It protects humans from electric shock and equipment from surge damage.

entries.title: Circuit Breaker & Fuse
entries.content: A circuit breaker automatically interrupts a circuit on overload/short-circuit and can be reset; a fuse melts once and must be replaced. MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) ratings: 6A lighting, 16A/20A power sockets typical homes. ELCB/RCD detects earth leakage (30 mA trip) and saves lives.
